source.title: Computing Nonvacuous Generalization Bounds for Deep (Stochastic) Neural Networks with Many More Parameters than Training Data

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and figure description; no apparent truncation affecting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports natural-label and random-label training/test errors on MNIST, conceptually bearing on coexistence of memorization capacity and generalization (V1), using a binary-class MNIST setup and reporting additional stochastic-network results.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports the study's own SGD train/test errors for true-label and random-label experiments. Appendix D reports error-bound behavior during SGD and path-norm regularization, but these are not held-out error-gap findings for the listed claim versions; cited results from other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests V1 in a new setting: a fully connected ReLU network on binary MNIST. Its own SGD results compare near-perfect fitting and held-out performance under natural and independently random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The principal contribution is nonvacuous PAC-Bayes bounds for stochastic networks obtained by optimizing around SGD solutions on binary MNIST. These bounds remain substantially looser than held-out error, and the random-label bound is vacuous. The authors leave explanations of deterministic SGD generalization and extension to other datasets and architectures open.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains fully connected ReLU MLPs on a binary-class variant of MNIST, then optimizes a PAC-Bayes bound; its natural/random-label comparison is not the original multi-class CIFAR-10 or ImageNet setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Label condition (true versus random) changes the reported test error; the study also varies depth and width for true-label architectures, but these comparisons do not test V2's width-beyond-interpolation claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizing Gaussian weight distributions produces nonvacuous PAC-Bayes error bounds of 0.161–0.223 for natural-label stochastic networks, while the random-label bound is vacuous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-dependent PAC-Bayes optimization can certify nontrivial generalization for overparameterized stochastic MLPs on binary MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D finds path-norm Rademacher bounds vacuous during ordinary SGD; sufficiently strong explicit regularization produces high training error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The evaluated path-norm bounds fail to certify useful generalization in these binary-MNIST experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The directly relevant experiment uses binary-class MNIST and a single small network for random labels; it does not test the named CIFAR-10 or ImageNet architectures. Test errors are empirical averages; the paper notes held-out Chernoff upper bounds are about 0.005 higher. The paper studies generalization bounds for stochastic perturbations, whose reported bounds are much looser than held-out error.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix D's path-norm error-bound plots and statements concern bounds becoming vacuous during training and do not report a result on any listed version's test-error gap or measured property; not included as rows. Other architectures in Table 1 are true-label-only comparisons and do not test a listed version beyond V1.

untested.parts: The named CIFAR-10 and ImageNet architectures and multiclass tasks are not tested; the random-label comparison covers only the one-hidden-layer, 600-unit network.
No width sweep establishes the interpolation threshold or trains wider networks to convergence beyond it; Table 1 uses fixed 20-epoch natural-label training.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison on the same training objective.
No comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps or competing measures in a convolutional family.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

record.verdict_notes: T3 best captures the new dataset and binary task; the relevant measurement remains ordinary SGD training/test classification error. The narrower experimental setting is an untested scope extension, not evidence against V1. The study is not an original source for V1.

versions.untested_parts: Tests one 600-hidden-unit MLP on binary-class MNIST, with random labels only for the small network; does not test the specified CIFAR-10 models or Inception V3 on ImageNet, and reports random-label test error rather than accuracy.

rows.subject: one 600-unit hidden layer (T-600)
rows.stage_stated: trained by SGD with momentum on true labels; 20 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Train a fully connected ReLU network on the binary-class variant of MNIST using true labels.
rows.measure: SGD classifier empirical train and test classification error
rows.note: Table reports empirical error. Model was trained for 20 epochs; the text says all true-label SGD networks achieved perfect or near-perfect training accuracy.
rows.check: No correction needed. Table 1 reports training error 0.001 and test error 0.018 for T-600.

rows.subject: one 600-unit hidden layer (R-600)
rows.stage_stated: trained by SGD with momentum on random labels; 120 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Train the same small network on independently uniform random binary labels.
rows.measure: SGD classifier empirical train and test classification error
rows.note: Random-label control. The paper describes test error 0.508 as representing lack of generalization, as expected.
rows.check: No correction needed. Table 1 reports training error 0.007 and test error 0.508 for R-600. Random-label training lasts 120 epochs versus 20 for natural labels; architecture, optimizer settings and batch size are otherwise shared.

relationships.condition: One-hidden-layer, 600-unit ReLU MLP trained with momentum SGD on binary MNIST, without explicit regularization
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show near-perfect training fit under both label conditions: natural-label test error is 0.018, while random-label test error is 0.508, approximately binary chance.
relationships.display_finding: Both labelings were fitted nearly perfectly, with test errors of 0.018 for natural labels after 20 epochs and 0.508 for random labels after 120 epochs.
